title: Avoiding TDS on EPF Withdrawal: Rules & Eligibility Explained
description: Withdrawing your Employees' Provident Fund (EPF) balance before completing five years of continuous service can lead to Tax Deducted at Source (TDS). TDS is t.

faq.q: ### What is the primary condition for TDS on EPF withdrawal?
faq.a: TDS is primarily applicable if you withdraw your EPF balance before completing five years of continuous service and the withdrawal amount exceeds ₹50,000.

faq.q: ### What is the TDS rate if I don't provide my PAN?
faq.a: If you do not provide your PAN, the TDS rate on EPF withdrawal will be a higher 20% instead of the standard 10%.

faq.q: ### Can Non-Resident Indians (NRIs) use Form 15G or 15H?
faq.a: No, Form 15G and Form 15H are specifically for resident Indians. NRIs cannot use these forms to avoid TDS on EPF withdrawals.

faq.q: ### Is interest earned on my EPF also subject to TDS if withdrawn prematurely?
faq.a: Yes, if withdrawn before five years, the entire accumulated balance, including employer contributions, employee contributions, and all interest earned on both, becomes taxable and subject to TDS.

faq.q: ### What if my employer's business closes down? Does TDS still apply?
faq.a: No, if your service is terminated due to the closure of the employer's business or any other reason beyond your control, TDS will not be deducted, even if your service period is less than five years.

faq.q: ### How do I check if my PAN is linked to my UAN?
faq.a: You can log in to the EPFO UAN member portal, navigate to the 'Manage' section, and then select 'KYC' to check the status of your PAN linking.

faq.q: ### If I transfer my EPF from one employer to another, does it break the continuous service period?
faq.a: No, transferring your EPF balance from your old employer's account to your new employer's account ensures continuity of service, and the combined period counts towards the five-year rule.
